rules: Volume correlated against a return-based term (ABS($return), or a 1-day volume delta) at a 21-day window gave this round's top two fitnesses (3.567, 2.616); the same idea against range ($high-$low) at 42 days failed the cheap screen. Keep pairing volume-correlation factors with return terms at ~21 days, not range terms at longer windows.

Standalone $dollar_volume trend features (rank-drift, argmax, delta) failed the cheap screen in all 3 tries this round; this family only works interacted with a fundamental signal, as in the accepted accrual_gap x dollar_volume-delta factor.

$asset_turnover combined with a 40-day return sum gave the two worst cheap-screen scores this round (0.09, 0.72); pair asset_turnover with other fundamentals or same-day range, not multi-week return sums.
COUNT of days volume or range exceeds its own trailing mean carried almost no signal in both attempts this round; use the continuous ratio or z-score instead of a threshold count.

Range-normalization factors ($high-$low over $dollar_volume, over $open, or via $low/$high min-max) each now have two neighboring windows tried (10&21, 63&126, 21&34); a window-only resubmission of these families will keep hitting archive_subtree or correlation, so change the core transform instead.

Adding an outer TS_DECAY_LINEAR or CS_ZSCORE around an already-archived ratio or z-score expression still shares 9+ nodes with it (3 rejections this round); vary the inner computation, since wrappers alone don't decorrelate.

The accrual_gap x dollar_volume and operating_margin/asset_turnover/leverage families already have close neighbors in the archive: a single added denominator or a rank-subtraction-to-ratio swap scored 0.84-0.86 correlation, not new signal. These need a different combinator, not an arithmetic tweak.

A nested TS_DELTA(TS_MEAN(field,N),N) shape and an overnight-gap x range product (($open - DELAY($close or $high,1)) times ($high-$low)) both collided with alpha101 canonical subtrees regardless of field; avoid re-deriving these two shapes on a new field.
